chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: First trip to Chicago with Uncle Willie
summary: In 1921 he went to Chicago with his grandmother and Uncle Willie, wandering Federal Street while his uncle found money in the gutter.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: No,, that was my second trip. I had been to Chicago in 1921 with my little uncle.

No, with Willie. My aunt went to visit my aunt, who lived in Chicago. He lived on 40th and State. And my grandmother went to visit, so she was taking Willie, the youngest boy -- so I wanted to go with Willie. My mother said, 'Well, we'll take you.' So they brought me up with him.
So what we used to do, we'd get up in the morning, like, around seven o'clock, after we (?). We'd go around back up on Federal Street, just bumming, you know, like kids...

And my uncle had this thing where he could walk in the gutter, you know, in the business section or something, walk around and pick up money. He'd walk in the street and see money, and I'd be right behind him, and I didn't see nothing! Ain't that somethin'?
